1.problem:
(See the diagram below.) \(ABCD\) is a square. Points \(G\), \(H\), \(I\), and \(J\) are chosen in the interior of \(ABCD\) so that:

  • (i) \(H\) is on \(\overline{AG}\), \(I\) is on \(\overline{BH}\), \(J\) is on \(\overline{CI}\), and \(G\) is on \(\overline{DJ}\);
  • (ii) \(\triangle ABH \cong \triangle BCI \cong \triangle CDJ \cong \triangle DAG\); and
  • (iii) the radii of the inscribed circles of \(\triangle ABH\), \(\triangle BCI\), \(\triangle CDJ\), \(\triangle DAK\), and \(GHIJ\) are all the same.

What is the ratio of \(\overline{AB}\) to \(\overline{GH}\)?
1.solutions: No official solution was published for this problem.

2.problem: The three solutions \(r_1\), \(r_2\), and \(r_3\) of the equation \[x^3 + x^2 - 2x - 1 = 0\] can be written in the form \(2\cos(k_1\pi)\), \(2\cos(k_2\pi)\), and \(2\cos(k_3\pi)\) where \(0 \le k_1 < k_2 < k_3 \le 1\). What is the ordered triple \((k_1, k_2, k_3)\)?
2.solutions: No official solution was published for this problem.

3.problem: \(\mathcal{P}\) is a convex polyhedron, all of whose faces are either triangles or decagons (10-sided polygon), though not necessarily regular. Furthermore, at each vertex of \(\mathcal{P}\) exactly three faces meet. If \(\mathcal{P}\) has 20 triangular faces, how many decagonal faces does \(\mathcal{P}\) have?
3.solutions: No official solution was published for this problem.

4.problem:
\(P_1\) is a parabola whose line of symmetry is parallel to the \(x\)-axis, has \((0,1)\) as its vertex, and passes through \((2,2)\).

\(P_2\) is a parabola whose line of symmetry is parallel to the \(y\)-axis, has \((1,0)\) as its vertex, and passes through \((2,2)\).

Find all four points of intersection between \(P_1\) and \(P_2\).
4.solutions: No official solution was published for this problem.
